docs.title: Choose a change source
docs.text:
This guide helps you pick how AlgoBridge learns that records changed in Salesforce, and switch to that source. The three sources differ in what you install in the org, in how many API requests they spend, and in how quickly a change arrives.

Every source ends in the same place: when an object has changed, AlgoBridge reads the changed records with a paged SOQL query. The source only decides how AlgoBridge finds out which objects to read. See Salesforce to PostgreSQL.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Salesforce is connected.
  • For the Apex probe or the change notifier: an admin who can deploy Apex to the org.
  • For the change notifier: PUBLIC_URL is an https:// address that Salesforce can reach.

docs.title: Compare the sources
docs.text:
Composite polling Apex probe Change notifier Installs in your org Nothing The AlgoBridge Apex bundle The same bundle, plus two Flows per synced object How it learns about changes Asks Salesforce on each poll whether each object changed Asks one class in your org, which checks up to 90 objects per request Your org tells AlgoBridge which objects changed, as it happens Requests per poll One per five objects One for up to 90 objects None; one fallback poll an hour Latency The poll interval The poll interval Near real time Needs inbound HTTPS to AlgoBridge No No Yes

Composite polling is the default.

docs.title: What each one costs
docs.text:
Daily API requests for 50 synced objects. The range covers poll intervals from 2 to 30 minutes.

Source Requests per day At a 5 minute interval Composite polling about 480 to 7,200 about 2,900 Apex probe about 48 to 720 about 290 Change notifier 0 to learn about changes, plus the fallback poll and 1 daily check about 25 with the Apex probe as fallback

The change notifier's fallback poll runs once an hour by default. It uses the Apex probe (24 requests a day) when the bundle is installed, or Composite polling (240 a day at 50 objects) otherwise. The notifier also uses one asynchronous Apex execution in your org per transaction that saves a synced object, from the org's daily allowance (the larger of 250,000 or 200 per user licence).

When the org nears its API limit, the budget governor widens every interval by four times, up to an hour, and Composite polling is the first to feel it. See API budget.

docs.title: When to pick each
docs.text:
• Composite polling if you can't deploy Apex, or you're trying AlgoBridge out. It works everywhere and needs no inbound access.
  • Apex probe for most production orgs. One deploy cuts polling requests by about ten times, needs no per-object setup, and nothing calls into AlgoBridge.
  • Change notifier when you need changes within seconds, or need the lowest API use, and AlgoBridge can accept HTTPS requests from Salesforce. You add two Flows by hand for each synced object.

docs.title: Switch the change source
docs.text:
1. Open Instance → Connections and scroll to Change detection.
  2. Read the three cards. Each lists what it installs, what it costs, its benefits and its limitations. The selected card is marked Selected.
  3. For the Apex probe or the change notifier, install the bundle: click Deploy bundle, then assign the permission set. See Install the Apex bundle.
  4. For the change notifier, click Pair notifier and add the Flows. See Pair the change notifier.
  5. Click Use this source on the card you want.

AlgoBridge verifies the source before saving it:

  • Composite polling has nothing to verify.
  • Apex probe makes one status call and checks that the bundle reports the expected version with the probe enabled.
  • Change notifier makes the same status call and checks that the notifier is installed and paired, that PUBLIC_URL uses https, and that this instance holds a live key.

If the check passes you see Change source saved. If not, Nothing was saved. The change source stays as it was. with the reason.

docs.title: Card states
docs.text: State Meaning Nothing to verify Composite polling. Verified 09:12 The last check passed at that time. Not verified yet No check has run since the source was chosen. Not installed: deploy the bundle The bundle is missing or too old. Not paired The notifier has no live key. Paired, key abk_…, last notification 12:40 The notifier is working.

docs.title: How a failing source is handled
docs.text:
A daily job checks the selected source at 02:20 UTC for one API request. If the source has become unusable, for example because someone deleted the Apex classes, AlgoBridge:

  • keeps polling with the next source down (change notifier, then Apex probe, then Composite polling),
  • opens the sf_change_source alert,
  • shows on Connections, for example: Selected: Apex probe. Unavailable since 12:40: … Running on Composite.

AlgoBridge never changes your selection by itself. Fix the cause, then click Use this source again to verify it.

docs.title: Watch it in the Live log
docs.text: These events appear in the Live log: sf_change_source_selected, sf_change_source_refused, sf_change_source_checked, and for the notifier notifier_paired, notifier_pair_failed, notifier_key_rotated, notifier_key_revoked, notifier_notification_accepted, notifier_notification_rejected and notifier_notification_not_selected.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Not installed: deploy the bundle

The status call found no bundle, or a bundle older than the one this release expects. Click Deploy bundle. See Install the Apex bundle.

The Apex probe reports an object as failed

The probe runs as the integration user, with sharing, in user mode. An object the integration user can't read is reported as failed. Give the user read access to the object, and check the AlgoBridge Integration permission set is assigned.

AlgoBridge must be reachable over HTTPS: set PUBLIC_URL to an https:// address.

The change notifier needs Salesforce to call AlgoBridge. Put AlgoBridge behind HTTPS, set PUBLIC_URL to that address, restart, and redeploy the bundle so its remote site matches.

This instance holds no live notifier key; pair the notifier again

The notifier keys were revoked or deleted, for example by disconnecting Salesforce. Click Pair notifier, then Use this source.

Changes made by the integration user don't arrive quickly

The change notifier ignores saves made by the integration user, so AlgoBridge's own writes don't echo back. Changes made under that user arrive on the hourly fallback poll instead. Use a dedicated integration user that people don't sign in as.

docs.title: Connect the client database
docs.text:
This guide connects your instance to the PostgreSQL database your application uses, the one AlgoBridge syncs with Salesforce. It also covers the privileges the database role needs, how the stored URL is protected, and how to rotate the encryption key.

The client database is separate from AlgoBridge's own platform database (DATABASE_URL), which holds the console's state and the job queue. An instance connects exactly one client database.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• PostgreSQL 15 or later, reachable from every container.
  • A database role for AlgoBridge with the privileges listed below.
  • Either ENCRYPTION_KEY set on every container, if you'll save the URL on screen, or access to set CLIENT_DATABASE_URL in your deployment.

docs.title: Required privileges
docs.text:
AlgoBridge creates its tables, trigger function and change log in a target schema (algobridge by default) when you apply a mapping. The role in the URL needs to:

  • Use the hstore extension. Either the extension is already installed in the database, or the role can create it.
  • Own the target schema, or be able to create it. On the first apply, the schema must contain no tables, views or other relations.

If a privilege is missing, the apply fails with a configuration error that names the missing grant. Nothing is changed in the database.

docs.title: Choose where the URL lives
docs.text:
Connections screen CLIENT_DATABASE_URL Needs ENCRYPTION_KEY Yes No Restart to change No Yes Shown on screen as Connected on this screen Set by the deployment (CLIENT_DATABASE_URL)

If CLIENT_DATABASE_URL is set, it wins. The screen can't save or disconnect a connection set by the deployment.

Warning

Setting CLIENT_DATABASE_URL on an instance that already has a URL saved on screen replaces the saved URL on the first check. The saved URL can't be recovered.

docs.title: Connect the database
docs.text:
On the Connections screenAs an environment variable

  1. Make sure ENCRYPTION_KEY is set on every container. Generate one with:

    openssl rand -base64 32

  2. Open Instance → Connections.

  3. In the PostgreSQL panel, enter the Connection URL, for example:

    postgres://app_user:change-me@db.example.com:5432/app?sslmode=require

  4. Click Test and connect.

AlgoBridge connects with a 5 second timeout and runs SELECT version(). If that works, it stores the URL encrypted and shows PostgreSQL connected. The URL was tested, then stored encrypted. If it fails, nothing is saved, and the error never contains the password.

  1. Set the URL in your deployment's secret store:

    CLIENT_DATABASE_URL=postgres://app_user:change-me@db.example.com:5432/app?sslmode=require

  2. Restart every container.

The panel reads Set by the deployment (CLIENT_DATABASE_URL). To use a different database, change the variable and restart.

After connecting, the panel shows only the host, port, database, user and SSL mode. The full URL is never shown again.

docs.title: Choose an SSL mode
docs.text:
Set sslmode in the URL:

sslmode Effect require Encrypts the connection. verify-full Encrypts, and also checks the server certificate and host name. not set No SSL. The panel shows Driver default.

Use verify-full when the server has a certificate your containers trust.

docs.title: Check the connection
docs.text:
Click Check connection to test the stored URL on demand. Each worker also checks it when it starts. The stamp shows:

Stamp Meaning Not checked No check has run yet. Healthy The last check connected. Unreachable The host could not be reached. Refused The server refused the login or the database.

docs.title: Replace the URL
docs.text:
1. In the PostgreSQL panel, enter the whole new URL in Replace with a new connection URL. You can't edit one part of the stored URL.
  2. Click Test and replace.

Your mappings are kept. The new database is tested first, and the stored URL changes only if the test passes.

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text:
1. Delete your mappings. Disconnect is refused while any exist.
  2. Click Disconnect, then Disconnect PostgreSQL in the dialog.

The stored URL is deleted and sync stops. Your tables and data stay in the database.

docs.title: Rotate the encryption key
docs.text:
ENCRYPTION_KEY protects every secret AlgoBridge stores: the client database URL, the Salesforce tokens, app credentials saved on screen, and change notifier secrets. To rotate it without losing any of them:

  1. Generate a new key:

    openssl rand -base64 32

  2. On every container, move the current key to ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS and put the new key in ENCRYPTION_KEY. Restart. AlgoBridge can now read secrets written with either key.

  3. Re-encrypt the stored secrets with the new key:

    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm app rotate-encryption-key

    Outside Docker, run node dist/cli/rotate-encryption-key.js. The command re-encrypts everything in one transaction and prints:

    Re-encrypted N stored secret(s) with key <id>. You can now remove ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS.

    The key id is the first 8 hex characters of the key's SHA-256 hash, so you can tell keys apart without printing them.

  4. Remove ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS from every container and restart.

ENCRYPTION_KEY_PREVIOUS is refused at startup unless ENCRYPTION_KEY is also set, and the two must differ.

docs.title: Deleting rows in synced tables
docs.text: AlgoBridge doesn't sync TRUNCATE. Truncating a read-write table deletes nothing in Salesforce. It also clears the algobridge_lastop and algobridge_err status columns. To delete records in Salesforce from PostgreSQL, use DELETE, in batches for large sets.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This is AlgoBridge's own database. Connect your application's database instead.

The URL points at the platform database, which holds the algobridge_jobs schema and the algobridge_migrations table. Use the URL of your application's database.

Set ENCRYPTION_KEY to store a connection.

Saving on screen needs an encryption key. Set ENCRYPTION_KEY on every container and restart, or set CLIENT_DATABASE_URL instead.

Enter a URL like postgres://user:password@host:5432/database.

The URL could not be parsed. Check the scheme, and percent-encode special characters in the password.

AlgoBridge could not connect with this URL.

The test connection failed within 5 seconds. Check the host, port, firewall rules, credentials and SSL mode from inside a container. Nothing was saved.

CLIENT_DATABASE_URL sets this connection. Change it in the deployment.

The deployment sets the URL, so the screen can't change it. Edit the variable and restart.

Delete your mappings first.

Disconnect is refused while mappings exist. Delete them on Sync → Mappings first.

Apply fails with a missing privilege

The role can't create the hstore extension, or doesn't own the target schema, or the schema already holds other relations on the first apply. Grant what the message names, or install hstore as a superuser, then apply again.

docs.title: Read the Live log
docs.text:
The Live log streams log lines from every AlgoBridge process into your browser as they happen. Use it to watch a sync step by step: each SOQL query, each Salesforce and PostgreSQL call, and each job, without access to the container logs.

The Live log keeps no history. Lines exist only in the open tab, so there is nothing to back up, export or purge. For the record of what synced, use Sync → Activity.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• You need the admin role (the logs.view permission). See Users and roles.
  • JavaScript must be on for the console. Without it, the page says The Live log needs JavaScript.

docs.title: Open the Live log
docs.text:
1. Open Instance → Live log. You can also click Open live log on Instance → Jobs & workers.
  2. The state pill in the page head changes from Connecting to following the stream, and lines start to arrive.

While at least one tab is open, every process in the deployment raises its log level to debug within about 5 seconds, so the tab shows every query and call, not only the lines your LOG_LEVEL normally keeps. When the last tab closes, the processes drop back within about 10 seconds.

Your container logs are not affected. Stdout always carries lines at LOG_LEVEL, whether anyone is watching or not.

What it costs

The Live log makes no Salesforce API calls. Each open tab holds one streaming connection to the web process and one connection to the platform database. Up to 5 people can watch at once; a sixth tab is told how many are already open and gets no stream. Allow one extra platform-database connection per admin who might watch.

docs.title: Read a line
docs.text: Each line shows the time, the level, the source, the process it came from and the message. Select a line to see its details, such as rows read, API calls made and how long the step took. Where a line belongs to a mapping or a job, the details link to Open mapping or Open Jobs & workers.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text: Level Shows Error Errors and fatal errors. Warn Warnings. Info Normal progress. Debug Debug and trace detail: every query, call and queue step.

docs.title: Sources
docs.text: Source Shows SOQL Salesforce queries. Salesforce Other Salesforce calls: writes, Bulk jobs, status checks. PostgreSQL Calls to the client database. Queue Job engine activity: jobs, ticks, queues, the watchdog and worker registration. Web The console's web process. Worker The sync worker.

docs.title: Filter the lines
docs.text:
Filters run in your browser and change only what you see. They don't change what the processes send.

  • Level and Source: click a toggle to hide or show those lines. Each level toggle shows how many lines it holds.
  • Process: show lines from one process, or All processes.
  • Mapping: show lines for one mapping, or All mappings.
  • Search lines: show only lines containing your text.

If nothing matches, the tab says No lines match these filters. Matching lines appear here as they happen.

docs.title: Follow, pause and copy
docs.text:
• The tab follows the newest line. Scroll back to stop following; Jump to latest takes you back.
  • Pause freezes the view while lines keep arriving in the background. Click Resume to catch up.
  • Copy lines copies the lines you see, or the lines you selected.
  • Clear empties the tab.

The tab keeps the newest 2,000 lines. Older lines are dropped from the tab as new ones arrive.

docs.title: What is hidden
docs.text:
• Values in SOQL string literals are masked as '…', except values shaped like record IDs.
  • Secrets such as tokens, passwords and keys are replaced with [redacted].

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The stream dropped

The tab shows Reconnecting and tries again by itself. Once it is back, a Disconnected at … UTC mark shows where lines may be missing. Streams are also renewed every 10 minutes, which you may notice as a brief reconnect.

The Live log could not connect.

The web process or the platform database didn't accept the stream. Check that the web container is healthy, and click Try again. If your session expired, sign in again.

Five people are already watching

The viewer limit is reached. Close a Live log tab elsewhere, or wait for someone else to close theirs.

Lines are missing during a busy sync

When more than 1,000 lines are waiting to be sent, AlgoBridge drops lines from the stream and logs a live_log_lines_dropped warning. The container logs are not affected, so check them for lines at your LOG_LEVEL.

I only see info lines

The level rises to debug within about 5 seconds of the tab opening. Wait a moment, and check that the Debug toggle is on.

docs.title: Create mappings
docs.text: A mapping syncs one Salesforce object with one PostgreSQL table. This guide shows you how to choose the object and its fields, create the table, run the initial load, and reload a table when you need a fresh copy.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Salesforce is connected and the client database is connected. Until both are, Sync → Mappings shows Connect Salesforce and PostgreSQL first.
  • Your user has the member or admin role. See Users and roles.
  • The database role can create the target schema and use hstore. See Required privileges.

docs.title: Step 1: Check the mapping settings
docs.text:
The Settings panel on Sync → Mappings applies to every mapping.

  • Target schema: the PostgreSQL schema AlgoBridge creates tables in. The default is algobridge. You can change it only until the first mapping exists. It must be a valid lowercase identifier (letters, digits and underscores, up to 63 characters) and can't be public, information_schema or start with pg_.
  • Write algorithm: how changes from PostgreSQL are sent to Salesforce. Ordered Writes (recommended) sends captured changes in order, one at a time, so a failed insert holds back only that record and rows that reference it. Merged Writes merges several changes to one record before sending, and sends parents ahead of children. See PostgreSQL to Salesforce.

Click Save after changing either.

docs.title: Step 2: Choose an object
docs.text:
1. Click New mapping.
  2. Search the list of objects, then click Choose on the one you want.

The list shows objects that can be queried and replicated, as of the time shown. Click Refresh if you've just created an object in Salesforce. Big objects (__b), platform events (__e) and external objects (__x) aren't listed. An object without a SystemModstamp field is shown as one that can't be synced, because AlgoBridge uses that field to find changed records.

docs.title: Step 3: Set direction and conflicts
docs.text:
• Direction:
    • Read-only (the default): Salesforce changes sync to PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL never writes back.
    • Read-write: changes also flow from PostgreSQL to Salesforce.
  • Conflict policy, for read-write mappings only: Salesforce wins (the default), PostgreSQL wins, or Latest change wins. See Conflicts.
  • Poll interval: set the fastest and slowest interval, between 2 and 60 minutes. The defaults are 5 and 30. While the object is quiet, the interval doubles after each poll that finds nothing, up to the slowest. A poll that finds a change resets it to the fastest.
  • External ID: for a read-write mapping, choose a Salesforce field that is marked both External ID and Unique. AlgoBridge uses it to match rows inserted in PostgreSQL to records, so a retried insert can't create a duplicate. Leaving it at None works, but the editor warns you about the risk.

docs.title: Step 4: Choose fields
docs.text:
The fields table lists each field's label, API name, Salesforce type and the PostgreSQL column type it becomes. Tick Sync for each field you want, and tick Indexed to add an index on its column.

  • Id becomes the sfid column. Id and SystemModstamp are always synced and can't be unticked. IsDeleted is added for you.
  • CreatedDate and Name are ticked by default.
  • Column names are the field's API name in lowercase, for example billingcity or invoice_total__c.
  • For a lookup, you can sync a field of the related record through its relationship. The column is named <relationship>__r__<field>, for example account__r__external_id__c. Polymorphic lookups don't offer this.
  • Column names longer than 63 bytes, a column named id, and any name starting with algobridge_ are refused.

docs.title: Field types
docs.text:
Salesforce type PostgreSQL type id, reference varchar(18) string, url, email, phone, encryptedstring varchar(length) picklist varchar(255) combobox varchar(length) multipicklist varchar(4099) textarea varchar(length) under 256, otherwise text boolean boolean int integer long bigint double, currency, percent numeric(precision, scale) date date datetime timestamptz time time anyType text

Compound fields (address, location) and base64 fields can't be selected. Sync their component fields instead, such as BillingCity.

docs.title: What is not synced
docs.text:
Formula fields are not synced. The editor lists them greyed out as Formula field — not synced, and a mapping that includes one is refused. Salesforce doesn't mark a record changed when only a formula's inputs change, so no polling source can keep a formula column correct. Compute the value in PostgreSQL instead, for example with a view or a generated column over the synced input fields.

The editor also warns you about:

  • more than 100 fields on one mapping,
  • encrypted fields, which may arrive masked if the integration user can't see them unmasked,
  • a lookup whose target object isn't mapped,
  • fields that changed in Salesforce since the mapping was saved, which are flagged Removed from Salesforce when they were deleted.

docs.title: Step 5: Save, then apply
docs.text:
1. Click Create mapping, or Save changes on an existing mapping. Saving changes nothing in your database.
  2. Review the Apply panel. It lists the exact statements AlgoBridge will run.
  3. Click Create table for a new mapping, or Apply changes for an edit.

A worker runs the statements in one transaction: if any of them fails, none of them stick, and the mapping shows failed with the statement that failed.

For every mapping, applying creates:

  • the target schema, if it doesn't exist,
  • the table, with a unique index on sfid, a unique index on the External ID column, and an index on each Indexed column.

For a read-write mapping, it also creates:

  • the hstore extension,
  • the change log table algobridge_change_log, and an archive kept for 30 days,
  • the trigger function algobridge_capture_change() and a trigger algobridge_capture on the table,
  • the status columns algobridge_lastop and algobridge_err.

Applying never drops or recreates a table, and never drops a column. A type change that would narrow a column is refused.

docs.title: Mapping states
docs.text: State Meaning draft Saved, not applied yet. provisioning Apply is running. active Syncing. paused Sync is stopped for this mapping. failed The last apply failed. The panel shows why.

docs.title: Step 6: Watch the initial load
docs.text:
When a mapping first becomes active, AlgoBridge loads every record of the object into the table.

It first counts the records, then picks the cheaper way to read them:

  • REST queries cost one request per 2,000 records.
  • Bulk API 2.0 costs about 5 requests plus one per 50,000 records.

Bulk is used only when it is strictly cheaper, so small objects load over REST. If Salesforce refuses a Bulk job, the load falls back to REST.

The mapping list shows progress, such as Loading 42%, and the mapping's Load panel shows rows read and the transport chosen. If the org is close to its API limit, the load waits and shows Waiting for API budget.

Adding fields to an active mapping works the same way: after you apply, the Load panel lists the new columns waiting to load and fills them from Salesforce.

To stop a load, click Stop load. Stopping keeps what has been read so far, and the panel shows Table may be incomplete — run Reload to finish.

docs.title: Reload a table
docs.text:
Reload empties the table and reads the whole object again. Use it after stopping a load, or when you want the table to match Salesforce exactly.

  1. Open the mapping and click Reload in the Load panel.
  2. The dialog shows how many rows the table holds. Type the table name to confirm.
  3. Click Reload table.

Before you reload, know that:

  • Salesforce wins. Changes made in PostgreSQL that haven't been sent yet are discarded, and rows with no sfid (inserted in PostgreSQL but not yet in Salesforce) are lost.
  • AlgoBridge runs TRUNCATE … RESTART IDENTITY inside the job. It never drops the table.
  • If another table has a foreign key to this one, Reload is refused. AlgoBridge never truncates with CASCADE.

docs.title: Daily reconciliation
docs.text: Once a day, at the hour set by reconcile_hour_utc (03:00 UTC by default), AlgoBridge compares every mapping with Salesforce using one Bulk query per mapping, about 5 requests each. Salesforce wins, and records deleted in Salesforce are deleted from the table. The sweep is deferred while the budget governor is slowing or pausing sync.

docs.title: Remove fields or a mapping
docs.text:
• Remove fields: untick them and save. The dialog Stop syncing these fields? reminds you that the columns and their data stay in PostgreSQL and simply stop being written. Click Stop syncing and save.
  • Delete a mapping: click Delete mapping. Choose Keep the table, or Drop the table and everything in it and type the table name to confirm.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Someone else changed this mapping. Reload to see their changes.

Another user saved the mapping after you opened it. Reload the page, check their changes, and make yours again.

Apply failed

The panel shows the statement that failed. The usual cause is a missing privilege on the client database, or a schema that already holds other tables on the first apply. See Required privileges.

Reload is refused because of a foreign key

Another table references this one. Drop or defer the foreign key, reload, then restore it.

The load stays on Waiting for API budget

The org's API usage is above the governor's threshold. The load continues once usage falls. See API budget.

A field I need is greyed out

It is a formula field, a compound field, or a base64 field. See What is not synced.

docs.title: Connect Salesforce
docs.text:
This guide connects your instance to one Salesforce org. You create an External Client App in Salesforce, give AlgoBridge its credentials, and sign in once as the integration user. After that, AlgoBridge refreshes its own tokens.

An instance connects exactly one org. To sync a second org, run a second instance.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• ENCRYPTION_KEY is set on every container (web and worker). AlgoBridge stores the OAuth tokens, and any app credentials saved on screen, encrypted with this key. Generate one with openssl rand -base64 32. See Configuration.
  • PUBLIC_URL is set to the address your browser uses to reach the console, for example https://sync.example.com. The OAuth callback is built from it.
  • You have a dedicated integration user in Salesforce. AlgoBridge signs in as this user and every call it makes runs as them. A dedicated user keeps the audit trail clear and matters later if you use the change notifier, which ignores the integration user's own saves.
  • You can create apps in Setup in the org.

docs.title: Choose where the app credentials live
docs.text:
The app's consumer key and secret can come from the console or from the deployment.

Connections screen Environment variables Where they're stored Encrypted in the platform database Your deployment's secret store How to change them Replace on screen Change the variables and restart Shown on screen as Saved on this screen Set by the deployment (SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID)

If both are set, the environment variables win.

docs.title: Step 1: Create the External Client App
docs.text:
1. In Salesforce, open Setup → External Client App Manager and create a new app.
  2. Name it AlgoBridge and enter a contact email.
  3. Turn on Enable OAuth.

  4. Set the Callback URL to your PUBLIC_URL followed by /connections/salesforce/callback, for example:

    https://sync.example.com/connections/salesforce/callback

    The Connections screen shows this exact URL with a Copy button.

  5. Add these OAuth scopes:

    • Manage user data via APIs (api)
    • Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access)
  6. Turn on Require PKCE.
  7. Leave Require secret for Web Server Flow on.
  8. Set the refresh token policy to valid until revoked. Rotating refresh tokens also works: AlgoBridge refreshes under a database row lock, so two processes never race for the same token.
  9. Save the app, then copy its Consumer Key and Consumer Secret.

Note

A new app can take a few minutes before Salesforce accepts sign-ins to it. If the first connect fails with a credentials error, wait and try again.

docs.title: Step 2: Give AlgoBridge the app credentials
docs.text:
On the Connections screenAs environment variables
  1. In the console, open Instance → Connections.
  2. In the Salesforce panel, paste the Consumer key and Consumer secret.
  3. Click Save app credentials.

The secret is stored encrypted and never shown again. To change it later, click Replace. Remove app credentials is available only after you disconnect the org.

  1. Set both variables in your deployment's secret store:

    SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID=change-me
SALESFORCE_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me

    Set them together. The app refuses to start if only one is set.

  2. Restart every container.

The panel now reads Set by the deployment (SALESFORCE_CLIENT_ID). To use a different app, change both variables and restart.

docs.title: Step 3: Connect the org
docs.text:
1. In the Salesforce panel, enter your My Domain URL:
    • Production: https://yourcompany.my.salesforce.com
    • Sandbox: https://yourcompany--sandbox.sandbox.my.salesforce.com
  2. Click Connect to Salesforce.
  3. Salesforce opens. Sign in as the integration user and allow access.
  4. You return to Connections with the notice Salesforce connected. Tokens are stored encrypted.

The panel now shows the org, its My Domain and org ID, the user AlgoBridge runs as, the instance, the API version, when tokens were last refreshed, and API usage today.

API cost

Token requests, token revokes and identity lookups don't count against the org's daily API limit. Check connection costs one API call: it reads the org's record and the current usage that Salesforce reports with the response. See API budget.

docs.title: Check the connection
docs.text:
Click Check connection at any time to confirm the tokens still work and to refresh the usage figures. The panel stamp shows one of these states:

Stamp Meaning Not connected No org is connected yet. Connected The tokens work. App changed The app credentials changed after the org was authorized. Reconnect to issue tokens to the new app. Reconnect needed Salesforce refused the stored tokens.

docs.title: Reconnect when authentication fails
docs.text:
Salesforce stops accepting the refresh token when it is revoked, when it expires under the app's policy, or when you change the app credentials. Sync then stops with an authentication error and the panel shows Reconnect needed or App changed.

  1. Open Instance → Connections.
  2. Click Reconnect in the Salesforce panel.
  3. Sign in as the same integration user, in the same org, and allow access.

You see Salesforce reconnected. New tokens are stored encrypted. Your mappings, and a paired change notifier, are kept, because the org is the same.

AlgoBridge refuses a reconnect that signs in to a different org. To change orgs, disconnect first.

docs.title: Disconnect
docs.text:
1. Delete your mappings. Disconnect is refused while any exist.
  2. Click Disconnect, then Disconnect Salesforce in the dialog.

AlgoBridge revokes the refresh token in Salesforce and deletes both stored tokens. Any change notifier keys are deleted too, so you must pair again after connecting.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Salesforce shows redirect_uri_mismatch

The callback URL in the app doesn't match the one AlgoBridge sends. Copy the URL from the Connections screen into the app exactly. It must use https and have no trailing slash. Check that PUBLIC_URL matches the address you use in the browser.

Salesforce rejected the consumer key or secret.

The key or secret is wrong, or the app is not usable yet. Copy both again from the app, click Replace, and wait a few minutes if the app is new.

The app must allow the refresh_token scope

Add Perform requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access) to the app's OAuth scopes and connect again.

This connect link expired. Start again.

More than 10 minutes passed between clicking Connect to Salesforce and returning, or the link was already used. Click the button again.

You signed in to a different org. Disconnect first to change orgs.

You signed in to an org other than the connected one. Sign in to the original org, or delete your mappings, disconnect and connect the new org.

Delete your mappings first.

Disconnect is refused while mappings exist. Delete them on Sync → Mappings, then disconnect.

Could not reach Salesforce.

The container has no outbound HTTPS route to Salesforce, or Salesforce is unavailable. Check outbound network access and try again.

Salesforce disconnected, but Salesforce didn't confirm the revoke

AlgoBridge deleted its tokens, but Salesforce didn't confirm the revoke. Revoke the token by hand in Setup → Connected Apps OAuth Usage.

The connection changed while you were confirming. Check it and try again.

Someone else changed the connection while your dialog was open. Reload the page and repeat the action.

docs.title: Set up sign-in
docs.text:
This guide sets up how people sign in to the console: AlgoBridge passwords with optional two-step verification, single sign-on through Google Workspace, Microsoft Entra ID, or any standard OpenID Connect provider, or a mix of them.

Sign-in is configured with environment variables, so each change needs a restart.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• PUBLIC_URL is set to the address people use, for example https://sync.example.com. Redirect URIs are built from it.
  • At least one admin exists. See Create the first admin.
  • For SSO: admin access to your identity provider, so you can register an application.

docs.title: How the settings fit together
docs.text:
Variable What it does AUTH_PROVIDERS Comma-separated list of sign-in methods: local, google, microsoft, oidc. For example local,google. Each SSO provider listed gets its own button. AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN Who may sign in with an AlgoBridge password: all (the default), admins or off. AUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS Optional. Email domains allowed to sign up on their first SSO sign-in, without an invite.

Rules that AlgoBridge checks at startup:

  • local must be in AUTH_PROVIDERS unless AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN=off.
  • AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN=off needs at least one SSO provider.
  • Each SSO provider's variables are required together. A deployment missing any of them refuses to start, so a half-configured provider can't go live.

docs.title: Local passwords and two-step verification
docs.text:
Local sign-in is on by default. Passwords are hashed with argon2id. There is no self-service "forgot password": an admin issues a set-password link from the Users page.

Two-step verification is optional and applies to local passwords only. It needs ENCRYPTION_KEY set, because the authenticator key is stored encrypted. Each person turns it on for themselves:

  1. Click your name at the top of the console to open Account.
  2. Under Two-step verification, click Set up.
  3. Scan the QR code with an authenticator app, or enter the key by hand. The key is shown once.
  4. Enter the 6-digit code the app shows and click Turn on.

From then on, signing in asks for a code after the password. If someone loses their authenticator, an admin can turn two-step verification off for them on the Users page.

docs.title: Add a single sign-on provider
docs.text:
The redirect URI for each provider is PUBLIC_URL followed by /auth/callback/<provider>. It must match exactly.

GoogleMicrosoftGeneric OIDC

Google sign-in accepts accounts from one Google Workspace domain.

  1. In the Google Cloud console, open APIs & Services → OAuth consent screen and set User type to Internal. This limits sign-in to your Workspace organization before AlgoBridge sees a login.
  2. Open APIs & Services → Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID.
  3. Choose Application type: Web application.

  4. Under Authorized redirect URIs, add:

    https://sync.example.com/auth/callback/google

  5. Save, and copy the Client ID and Client secret.

  6. Set these variables and restart:

    AUTH_PROVIDERS=local,google
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=change-me
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
GOOGLE_HOSTED_DOMAIN=example.com

AlgoBridge checks Google's hosted-domain (hd) claim on every sign-in and accepts only GOOGLE_HOSTED_DOMAIN. Personal Gmail accounts never carry it, so they're always refused.

Microsoft sign-in accepts accounts from one Entra ID tenant.

  1. In the Entra admin center, open Identity → Applications → App registrations → New registration.
  2. Choose Accounts in this organizational directory only (Single tenant).

  3. Under Redirect URI, choose platform Web and enter:

    https://sync.example.com/auth/callback/microsoft

  4. Open Certificates & secrets → New client secret. Copy the value, which is shown once, and note its expiry date. Rotate it before it expires, or sign-in stops working.

  5. From the app's Overview, copy the Application (client) ID and the Directory (tenant) ID.
  6. Open Token configuration → Add optional claim, choose token type ID, and add email and xms_edov.

  7. Set these variables and restart:

    AUTH_PROVIDERS=local,microsoft
MICROSOFT_CLIENT_ID=change-me
MICROSOFT_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID=00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000

MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID must be your tenant's GUID. common, organizations and consumers are refused at startup, because they would admit accounts from any tenant.

Don't skip the optional claims

Entra's email claim alone isn't guaranteed to be verified. AlgoBridge trusts it only with xms_edov: true. Without both claims, an invited user's first Microsoft sign-in is refused, because there is no verified email to match the invite.

Use this for Okta, Keycloak, Auth0 or any other standard OpenID Connect provider. The provider must support:

  • discovery at <issuer>/.well-known/openid-configuration,
  • the authorization code flow with PKCE (S256),

  • ID tokens with email and email_verified, where email_verified is the boolean true. A string "true" counts as unverified.

  • In your provider, create an OIDC web application and register this redirect URI:

    https://sync.example.com/auth/callback/oidc

  • Note the issuer URL, client ID and client secret. Typical issuer URLs:

    Provider Issuer URL Okta https://example.okta.com/oauth2/default Keycloak https://<keycloak-host>/realms/<realm-name> Auth0 https://<your-tenant>.auth0.com/

  • Set these variables and restart:

    AUTH_PROVIDERS=local,oidc
OIDC_ISSUER=https://example.okta.com/oauth2/default
OIDC_CLIENT_ID=change-me
OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET=change-me
OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME=Okta
OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS=example.com

OIDC_ISSUER must use https. The button reads Continue with followed by OIDC_DISPLAY_NAME.

Set OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS to the domains you control. A generic provider might assert a verified email for a domain it doesn't own, and this list limits which emails can link to an account or sign up. Matching is exact: a subdomain isn't covered.

You can list several providers at once, for example AUTH_PROVIDERS=local,google,oidc. The sign-in page shows one button per provider.

docs.title: Limit password sign-in
docs.text:
Once SSO works, set:

AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN=admins

This is the recommended setting with SSO. Only admins can still sign in with a password, as a break-glass path. Everyone else uses the provider button. A non-admin's correct password is refused.

AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN=off removes the password form entirely.

The create-admin command and admin-issued set-password links keep working in every mode, including off.

docs.title: How accounts are matched
docs.text:
People sign in through SSO with an account that already exists in AlgoBridge:

  • Invited users are matched by verified email on their first SSO sign-in. Invite them on the Users page first.
  • Existing password accounts with the same verified email are linked on the first SSO sign-in from that provider, including accounts with two-step verification on. After that, the account accepts either way of signing in. SSO sign-ins never ask for a two-step code: the provider's own sign-in security stands in for it.
  • Just-in-time sign-up: if the person has no account and their email domain is in AUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS, AlgoBridge creates one with the viewer role.

Warning

If you have password accounts you don't want linked to SSO, disable or rename them before you turn a provider on.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
These notices appear on the sign-in page.

That account is not part of the organization this console accepts.

Google: the hd claim was missing or didn't match GOOGLE_HOSTED_DOMAIN, usually a personal account. Microsoft: the token's tenant didn't match MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID. Generic OIDC: the email domain isn't in OIDC_ALLOWED_EMAIL_DOMAINS.

Your identity provider did not confirm your email address…

The ID token had no verified email. For Microsoft, add the email and xms_edov optional claims. For generic OIDC, request the email scope and check that the provider sends email_verified as a boolean.

Your account is not set up in AlgoBridge yet.

No user is invited with this email, and AUTH_ALLOWED_DOMAINS doesn't cover it. An admin can invite the person on the Users page.

This account is disabled.

An admin can enable the account on the Users page.

This AlgoBridge account is already linked to a different sign-in from that provider.

The AlgoBridge account is already tied to another identity from the same provider. An admin has to resolve this; unlinking isn't self-service yet.

Sign-in with your identity provider did not complete.

The provider returned an error, for example because consent was denied. Try again, and check the application settings in the provider if it persists.

Your sign-in took too long or was already used.

More than 10 minutes passed, or the sign-in was already completed once. Click the provider button again.

Your identity provider could not be reached.

AlgoBridge couldn't reach the provider's discovery or token endpoint. Wait and try again. Admins can still sign in with a password unless AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN=off.

The container refuses to start

A provider is listed in AUTH_PROVIDERS without all its variables, MICROSOFT_TENANT_ID isn't a GUID, OIDC_ISSUER isn't https, or AUTH_LOCAL_LOGIN conflicts with AUTH_PROVIDERS. The startup error names the variable.

docs.title: Manage users and roles
docs.text:
This guide shows you how to create the first admin, invite people, give each one the right role, and handle lost passwords and authenticators.

Each person has exactly one role. Roles are fixed: there is no role editor.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The platform database is migrated. See Install.
  • To email invitations, set SMTP_URL (smtp:// or smtps://) and SMTP_FROM together. Without them, AlgoBridge shows each link to the admin once, to pass on yourself.
  • If people will sign in through SSO, set that up first. See Set up sign-in.

docs.title: Roles and what they allow
docs.text:
Role Can viewer See sync status, mappings, activity and errors, and the Jobs & workers page. member Everything a viewer can, plus create, edit and delete mappings, retry failed records, and operate sync (retry, cancel, redrive and dismiss jobs). admin Everything, including connections, users and the Live log.

The permissions behind each role:

Permission viewer member admin sync.view ✓ ✓ ✓ errors.view ✓ ✓ ✓ records.retry ✓ ✓ sync.operate ✓ ✓ mappings.manage ✓ ✓ mappings.delete ✓ ✓ connections.manage ✓ users.manage ✓ settings.manage ✓ logs.view ✓ alerts.receive ✓ webhooks.manage ✓ tokens.manage ✓ audit.view ✓

Pages a person can't use are hidden from their navigation.

docs.title: Create the first admin
docs.text:
The first admin is created from the command line, on the server.

  1. Run the migrations, if you haven't:

    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm app migrate

  2. Create the admin:

    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm app create-admin --email you@example.com --name "Your Name"

    Outside Docker, run node dist/cli/create-admin.js with the same options.

  3. The command prints a set-password link once. Open it, choose a password, and sign in.

The link works once and expires in 7 days.

docs.title: Invite a person
docs.text:
1. Open Instance → Users and click Invite person.
  2. Enter their Email, optionally their Name, and choose a Role.
  3. Click Create invite link.

What happens next depends on how they sign in:

  • Password sign-in: they get a set-password link that works once and expires in 7 days. With SMTP set, it is emailed: Invitation emailed. The link works once and expires in 7 days. Without SMTP, the page shows the link with Copy link. It isn't shown again.
  • SSO: they click their provider's button. AlgoBridge matches the invite by verified email.

Invited users show as Invited until they accept. If the link expires, the row shows Link expired: click New link.

docs.title: Change a role
docs.text:
Click Change next to the person's role, pick the new role, and save.

You can't change your own role. Another admin has to.

docs.title: Reset a password
docs.text:
There is no self-service "forgot password". To reset one:

  1. On Instance → Users, click Reset link for the person.
  2. Send them the link, or let SMTP email it.

The link works once and expires in 7 days. A disabled user can't get a link until you enable them.

docs.title: Turn off two-step verification for someone
docs.text:
If a person loses their authenticator:

  1. Click Turn off two-step on their row.
  2. Confirm with Turn off.

They are signed out everywhere, any outstanding links are revoked, and they sign in with their password alone. They can set two-step verification up again from Account. This isn't offered for SSO users, who don't use AlgoBridge codes.

docs.title: Disable and enable users
docs.text:
Click Disable to stop a person signing in. Their sessions end immediately. Users are never deleted.

Click Enable to let them back in. If they never set a password, send them a new link.

docs.title: Rules that protect access
docs.text:
• You can't change your own role or disable yourself.
  • The last active admin can't be demoted or disabled. Make another user an admin first.
  • The create-admin command works in every sign-in mode, so you can always recover access. If you're locked out, create another admin with a new email address.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
This is the last active admin. Make another user an admin first.

Promote someone else to admin, then change or disable this account.

You cannot change your own role or status. Ask another admin.

Ask another admin, or create one with create-admin.

This person has not accepted their invitation yet. Send them a new link instead.

The person hasn't set a password yet, so there's nothing to reset. Click New link.

A disabled user cannot get a set-password link. Enable them first.

Click Enable, then send the link.

Link not valid

Password links work once and expire after 7 days. Ask an admin for a new one.

docs.title: Run workers and jobs
docs.text:
This guide shows you how to split the console and the sync work into separate containers, scale workers, stop them safely, and read the Jobs & workers page when something gets stuck.

All background work, such as sync ticks, loads, the watchdog and cleanup, runs as jobs in PostgreSQL. The jobs live in the algobridge_jobs schema of the platform database. There is no Redis, broker or external queue to run. See Architecture.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• AlgoBridge is installed and the platform database is migrated. See Install.
  • You can set environment variables and restart containers in your runtime.

docs.title: Choose a role for each container
docs.text:
APP_ROLE decides what a container does:

APP_ROLE Serves the console Runs jobs all Yes Yes web Yes No worker No Yes

A single all container is enough for most installs. Run web and worker containers separately when you want to scale the console and the sync work independently, or keep sync running while you restart the console.

Every container, whatever its role, needs the same DATABASE_URL and the same ENCRYPTION_KEY.

docs.title: Split web and worker
docs.text:
1. Run the migrate role once for the version you're deploying:

    docker compose -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm app migrate

    Outside Docker, run node dist/cli/migrate.js. It applies the platform migrations and installs or upgrades the job schema. It is safe to run more than once.

  2. Start one or more containers with APP_ROLE=web, behind your load balancer.

  3. Start one or more containers with APP_ROLE=worker. Workers need outbound access to Salesforce and the client database, but no inbound traffic.
  4. Open Instance → Jobs & workers and check that each worker appears under Workers with its role.

A container that starts before migrate has run refuses to boot with The job schema is not installed. Run the migrate role first.

docs.title: Scale workers
docs.text:
Workers share the queues. Each sync key runs on one worker at a time, so adding workers spreads keys across them rather than running a key twice. If a worker dies mid-job, another worker takes the job over, usually within 16 to 25 seconds.

Each container polls the platform database every 2 seconds. That costs a few cheap queries per container, so run as many workers as the sync load needs and no more.

docs.title: Stop a container safely
docs.text:
On SIGTERM, a worker stops taking new jobs and lets the running ones finish, for up to 30 seconds. It then marks itself stopped and closes its connections.

Give every container a stop timeout longer than 30 seconds, so your runtime never kills it first:

Docker ComposeDockerKubernetes 
services:
  app:
    stop_grace_period: 45s

The file in deploy/docker-compose.yml already sets this. Keep it when you copy the file. The Compose default is 10 seconds.

docker stop --time 45 <container>

The default is 10 seconds.

spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 45

The default is 30 seconds, exactly the drain deadline, so set it explicitly.

On any other runtime, set its stop or drain timeout to 45 seconds or more.

If a container is killed before it finishes draining, its jobs are taken over once their heartbeat lapses, and its worker row shows as online until it goes stale.

docs.title: Upgrade
docs.text:
1. Run migrate for the new version.
  2. Roll out the web and worker containers.

Workers drain and hand over as described above, so a rolling restart doesn't lose work.

docs.title: Read the Jobs & workers page
docs.text:
Instance → Jobs & workers shows:

  • Workers: each worker's role, host, start time, last seen time and jobs in flight.
  • Queues: per-queue counts of waiting, active and retrying jobs, completed and failed in the last 24 hours, and the queue's state.
  • Jobs: the job list, filtered by state (waiting, active, retrying, failed, completed, cancelled) and queue, with each job's key, retries and last error.
  • Engine warnings from the last 24 hours.

The page refreshes every 5 seconds while the tab is visible. Job payloads are never shown.

Everyone can see the page. Members and admins can also retry, cancel, redrive and dismiss.

docs.title: Queue states
docs.text: State Meaning healthy Jobs are being picked up on time. backlog Some ready jobs have waited more than 30 seconds. failing A job in this queue failed in the last 24 hours. idle No jobs in the last 24 hours. dead letter The dead letter queue holds jobs.

docs.title: Notices in the navigation
docs.text:
Every page marks Jobs & workers in the navigation when something needs attention:

  • No worker is running. Sync is paused. with a ! badge: a worker has run before, and none has checked in for 30 seconds. Start a worker or all container.
  • N jobs in dead letter: jobs used up their retries. Open the page, read the last error, fix the cause, then redrive.

docs.title: Handle dead letter jobs
docs.text:
A sync tick that fails five times moves to the dead letter queue. Meanwhile, the watchdog runs once a minute and restarts any sync key that has no queued tick, so sync resumes before anyone acts.

  1. Open Instance → Jobs & workers and read the Last error of the dead letter jobs.
  2. Fix the cause, for example a revoked Salesforce token or a missing database privilege.
  3. Click Redrive on the queue and confirm with Redrive jobs. The jobs go back to their original queues.
  4. If the notice says some jobs were left, their sync key is already queued or running again. Click Dismiss and confirm with Dismiss jobs. Dismissed jobs are cancelled and kept, with their last error, under the cancelled state until retention removes them.

A sync key that fails with a configuration or authentication error isn't retried as usual. The watchdog restarts it within a minute, so it retries about once a minute until you fix the problem.

docs.title: Retention
docs.text:
• Completed and failed jobs are kept for 14 days, then deleted.
  • Worker rows silent for an hour are pruned hourly. The most recent one is always kept.
  • Salesforce API usage rows older than 30 days are pruned hourly.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
The job schema is not installed. Run the migrate role first.

Run migrate for this version, then start the container again.

No worker is running. Sync is paused.

No worker or all container has checked in for 30 seconds. Start one, and check its logs if it exits at boot.

Another job for that key is already queued or running

You tried to retry or redrive a job whose sync key already has a job, usually because the watchdog restarted it. Dismiss the old job instead.

A worker still shows as online after it stopped

It was killed before it could mark itself stopped. Its jobs are taken over once their heartbeat lapses, and the row goes stale. Raise the container's stop timeout to 45 seconds.

The same error repeats about once a minute

A configuration or authentication error is being retried by the watchdog. Read the error on the page or in the Live log and fix the cause, for example reconnecting Salesforce.
